slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
A reflection across line m maps each point P to P' so that m is the perpendicular bisector of PP'. Points on m map to themselves.

To reflect a polygon with compass and straightedge, drop a perpendicular from each vertex to m and extend it the same distance past m. In coordinates, reflecting across the x-axis gives (x, −y), across the y-axis (−x, y), and across y = x gives (y, x). A reflection reverses orientation: clockwise labels become counterclockwise.
